name: Google Workspace
description: Connect Gmail, Calendar, Drive and more to CliDeck. Choose which projects and agents can use each Google account.

commands.name: status
commands.description: List accounts permitted for this agent in its current project. Downloads gog if missing; --check verifies credentials with Google. Otherwise account metadata stays local.

commands.name: setup
commands.description: To connect an account before access is granted, use connect-request with email, services and readonly on stdin. The user approves the exact agent/project in CliDeck and signs in with Google; connect-status polls your request by id. Other setup actions require existing account access. JSON fields go on stdin; never put credentials or OAuth callback addresses in argv. Inspect google/status for services, clients and sign-in progress. Later sign-in failures return to the initiating agent.

commands.name: help
commands.description: Read the installed gog command help. Discover actual commands and flags before using them.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Run a Google service command using an allowed account. One allowed account is automatic; otherwise use the project default or explicit --account (and --client if needed). If denied, ask the user to assign access in Configure; never bypass with direct gog. JSON and non-interactive by default; stdin and caller directory are preserved.

settings.label: gog location
settings.description: Usually leave empty. CliDeck finds or prepares the Google connection automatically. Set a full executable path only for a custom installation.

settings.label: OAuth client
settings.description: Leave empty to use CliDeck’s built-in Google connection. Set a named custom OAuth client only if you manage your own Google app.
